page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor architecture running at 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration features 256 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Network performance is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 98066.33 and Geekbench multi-core reaching a top-tier score of 21018.0. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, registering a top-tier PassMark memory score and strong read-only large block bandwidth of 254.06 GB/sec. The server excels in software compilation, scoring 59722.0 in Geekbench clang compilation, and shows strong database capabilities with 103.12 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. However, single-core performance is average, and text generation for small LLM models is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the poor tier at 28.18 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture eliminates virtualization overhead, maximizing resource density for multi-threaded workloads. The inclusion of 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage bundled directly with the instance provides high-speed, low-latency data access without the added cost of external block storage. This makes the server highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, static web serving, and high-throughput database operations.
